viva_questions.q: What does the ‘K’ in K-Means represent, and who chooses it?
viva_questions.a: K represents the predefined number of clusters, chosen by the practitioner before running the algorithm.

viva_questions.q: What happens to WCSS as K approaches n (number of data points)?
viva_questions.a: WCSS drops monotonically to 0, because every single point becomes its own centroid.

viva_questions.q: Why does random initialisation sometimes give a worse clustering than k-means++?
viva_questions.a: Random initialisation can pick centroids in the same cluster, leading to poor local minima. K-means++ spreads out initial seeds using distance-weighted probability.

viva_questions.q: If a(i) > b(i) for a point, what does that tell you about its cluster assignment?
viva_questions.a: s(i) becomes negative, meaning the point is closer to a neighboring cluster than its assigned cluster (likely misclassified).
